title: Early release scheme won't work without us, says ex-prisoner

input.lead: Jamie Dale spent more than 11 years in prison and now runs a support network for former inmates
input.summary: Jamie Dale spent more than 11 years in prison and now runs a support network for former inmates
input.evidence_text: A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison" "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said

title: Middleton residents campaign to keep beloved kickpitch

input.lead: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
input.summary: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
input.evidence_text: Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational."

input.evidence_text: Plot targeting Manchester Jewish community disrupted, say police - BBC News Image caption, Two suspects were detained in Manchester city centre on Sunday, police said By Lauren Hirst , North West and Lucy Manning , Special correspondent Published 22 September 2026 Two men have been arrested over a suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester, police have said. The men, both in their 30s, were arrested on Sunday on the eve of Yom Kippur - considered to be the holiest day in the Jewish calendar - when thousands of British Jews were in synagogues already guarded with a heavy security and police presence. The men were detained on suspicion of offences under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000, according to the Metropolitan Police, which is leading the investigation. Sources have told the BBC the suspected plot was "fairly imminent" and in the later stages of planning. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the government would "continue to do all in our power to address threats against our Jewish community". She added: "We cannot expect our Jewish community to live behind higher walls. "We must also tackle antisemitism at its source and root it out wherever it rears its head." 'Remain viligant' Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said police were aware the news would cause "further concern" to the Jewish community "especially given the significant High Holy day period". The two suspects remain in police custody after being taken to a London police station for questioning. Police said the investigation related to a "suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in the Manchester area". title: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire

input.summary: Staffordshire Police was called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Elbit Systems, on Monday
input.evidence_text: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, Staffordshire Police was called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Elbit Systems, in Shenstone on Monday Published 22 September 2026 Nine people opposed to Israel's military action in Gaza have been arrested after a protest at a drone factory. Police were called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Israeli firm Elbit Systems, in Shenstone, Staffordshire, at 06:40 BST on Monday. Four people were held on suspicion of the charge of "lock on to person/object/land to cause serious disruption". They are two men aged 57 and 73 from the Stroud area of Gloucestershire; a 39-year-old woman of no fixed address; and a 77-year-old man from the Bolton area. A man, 55, of no fixed address, was arrested on suspicion of wilful obstruction on a highway. Four others were questioned on suspicion of both offences, Staffordshire Police said. They are a 74-year-old woman from Powys, mid Wales; a 63-year-old woman from the Radstock area in Somerset, a 30-year-old woman from Basildon, Essex; and a 24-year-old woman from London. The police force said protest activity in the area had finished and inquiries were continuing. input.evidence_text: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount Offenders caught committing fly-tipping offences will now face a £1,000 fine, an increase from the current £700 penalty. Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. A total of 992 fines were issued for waste deposits in the same period The strategy supports the aims of the council's Our Manchester Strategy , which sets out a vision for cleaner, greener and better maintained neighbourhoods

title: New Bolton Museum exhibition celebrates the art of Dame Laura Knight - Bolton Council

input.evidence_text: The new exhibition Laura Knight: The Art of Community opens at Bolton Museum on Saturday 19 September The exhibition brings together the museum’s small but significant collection of works by the pioneering British artist This is the first time that the four paintings and one drawing have been shown together in one gallery Dame Laura Knight (1877-1970) is one of Britain’s best-loved artists whose career spanned 70 years and encompassed a huge variety of subjects, techniques, and styles Her achievements were many: she was the first female artist to be elected as a full member of the Royal Academy, she was a prominent war artist in both World Wars, and she was made a Dame in 1929 for her services to art The exhibition at Bolton Museum includes her celebrated painting, The Fishing Fleet , from 1900, with the dramatic work depicting the working life of the fishing community in Staithes

We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club , or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! . . . . . Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. . . . . We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument.. . . Snacks and drinks provided, and pizzas on the final day. Please bring your own packed lunch to sessions Monday-Thursday.. . Dates: Monday 17th – Friday 21st August. Times: 10:00-16:30 Monday-Thursday, then a performance for friends and family on Friday at 13:00 (students will be expected to come in at 10:00 sharp on the Friday).. Ages: 12-18 years old.
